transcript.text:
Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. When a tumble dryer appears to stop working properly—often by running but not drying, or cutting out—it is very frequently caused by restricted airflow rather than a major mechanical failure. The most common culprit is a blocked lint filter or condenser unit. If the airflow is restricted, the dryer can overheat and trigger a safety cut-out that stops the heating element to prevent damage. This means the drum might still turn, but no warm air is produced. Please do this simple check first:
1. Locate the lint/fluff filter (usually inside the door frame) and remove it.
2. Check if it is clogged with fluff or debris. If so, clean it thoroughly under running water if possible, let it dry completely, and refit it.
3. If your dryer has a condenser unit (often behind a flap at the bottom front), remove it and rinse off any fluff buildup under the tap. Let it drip-dry before putting it back. Once you have done this, try running a normal heat programme for 10–15 minutes to see if warm air is produced. Was the filter or condenser unit full of fluff when you checked it?
Haven't looked at the filter yet. But the lights come on and nothing happens at all when I press start, no sound. Door also doesn't seem to click shut.

The fact that the lights come on but nothing happens when you press start, combined with the door not clicking shut, points strongly to a mechanical issue with the door handle or catch. The dryer has a safety switch that prevents it from starting unless the door is firmly latched; if the catch is broken or something is blocking it, the machine will sit idle. Please do this check:
1. Open the door and ensure no clothing is trapped in the seal.
2. Close the door firmly until you hear a distinct click.
3. Press start again. If it starts now, the issue was just something blocking the latch or the handle not engaging fully. If it still does nothing, we will need to look at the door switch itself.

Tried that. It won't click, the door swings back slightly open. The plastic tongue on the door has snapped off, found the bit on the floor. If I hold the door firmly shut and press start it runs, but stops when I let go.

That suggests it is a mechanical fault with the door handle or catch. The plastic tongue that engages with the cabinet has snapped off, so the machine cannot tell the door is shut and will not start for safety reasons. This is a standard repair part available from appliance spare parts suppliers using your model number. 1. Locate the model number on the rating plate or inside the door frame.
2. Search for "door handle" or "door latch assembly" for that specific model.
3. Once you have the part, replacement usually involves removing the top panel and/or the front panel to access the mounting screws for the handle. If you are not comfortable dismantling the front of the machine, this is a job for an engineer or a competent DIYer with some experience in appliance repair.
